findings.description: The footer copyright text is left in English on the French landing page instead of being translated.
The hero subtitle uses the informal "tu" form (Découvre tes) while the rest of the site (e.g., navigation, buttons) uses the formal "vous" register, creating an inconsistent register.
The validation error for the full name field is shown in English, while all other field validation errors on the same form are correctly translated to French.

findings.observed: Merci. Votre demande pour {montant} a été reçue.
findings.expected: Merci. Votre demande pour 5 000,00 $ a été reçue.
findings.description: The confirmation message on the French application summary page shows the unresolved template placeholder "{montant}" instead of the formatted loan amount, while the English version correctly shows "$5,000.00".

The checkbox labeled "Pay later" in English is translated as "Payer maintenant" (Pay now) in French, reversing its meaning. The help text below it still correctly describes a deferred first payment, contradicting the checkbox label.

The estimated monthly payment amount uses English currency formatting ($450.91) instead of the Canadian French convention (450,91 $), unlike other amounts on the site such as "5 000,00 $" on the application summary page.

findings.expected: Taux variable de 5,2 %, sous réserve de l'approbation du crédit.
findings.description: The French rate note omits the qualifier "subject to credit approval" that is present in the English version ("Variable rate of 5.2%, subject to credit approval.").
The modal's close button, labeled "Close" in English, is translated as "Proche" (meaning "near/close by" as an adjective) instead of the verb "Fermer" used to close a dialog.

findings.observed: Aucune accusation pour un remboursement anticipé.
findings.expected: Aucuns frais ne s'appliquent pour un remboursement anticipé.
findings.description: "Accusation" is a false cognate for the English "charges" (fees); in French "accusation" means a legal accusation/charge against someone, not a monetary fee. The correct term is "frais".
The "Recent transactions" section heading on the French dashboard is left untranslated in English, while the summary count just above it correctly reads "3 opérations récentes".
The "Estimer un nouveau prêt" link on the French dashboard page points to the English version of the calculator page (/en/calculator) instead of staying in French.

Transaction dates on the French dashboard are shown in US MM/DD/YYYY format (e.g. 09/15/2026), whereas the English version uses ISO format (2026-09-15). Canadian French convention uses YYYY-MM-DD or DD/MM/YYYY, not the US format.

The field label uses the anglicism "e-mail" while the validation error message for the same field correctly uses the Quebec French term "courriel" ("Entrez une adresse courriel valide."), creating inconsistent terminology.

findings.observed: Image text reads "Taux fixe : 4,9 %" but alt text and surrounding page text say "Taux variable : 5,2 %"; English version's image correctly reads "Variable rate: 5.2%" matching its alt text.
findings.expected: Image should display "Taux variable : 5,2 %" matching the alt text and the rest of the page content.
findings.description: The French promo banner image (promo-c.png) shows completely different text and a different rate ("Taux fixe : 4,9 %" - Fixed rate: 4.9%) than its alt attribute ("Taux variable : 5,2 %") and the rest of the page, which consistently refer to a 5.2% variable rate. This is a wrong image asset being used for the French locale.
